text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Bonn and regional government for state of Brandenburg agree aid measures for flood-hit eastern Germany.
- Government report on state of German unity says former east Germany has received almost 1,000 billion marks in transfers.
- Government statistics record 44 percent increase in first-time users of hard drugs in first half of 1997.
- Domestic shipping firms hit by flood wave.
- Rent prices continue decline begun two years ago, German estate agents say.
HANDELSBLATT
- Stock markets record record rises, taking cue from United States.
- Profits at software firm SAP rise faster than turnover.
- Deutsche Bank shows hefty rise in profits for first half of 1997.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel considers plan to cap Germany's contributions to the European Union.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Dyke bursts on Oder river, forcing thousands to flee their homes.
- DAX share index records third-biggest jump of all time.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem expects pension contributions to rise next year.
- Employers' federation president Hans-Olaf Henkel criticises government economic policy.
DIE WELT
- German blood products are now safest in the world, health officials say.
- Progress reported in talks between ruling coalition and opposition Social Democrats on reforming tax system.
- Latest figures show 55.1 million vehicles registered in Germany on June 1 this year.
